procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 26.04.2022 of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in WP No.411 of 2021.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court dismissed a writ petition (WP No. 411 of 2021) seeking transfer of the investigation of FIR No. 120 of 2020 to the CBI and/or any other agency. The High Court opined that the investigating agency had conducted the investigation from all angles by filing the chargesheet/supplementary chargesheet, considered the medical report, and collected the CRD of the Mobile Phone. The High Court also stated that once charges have been framed by the Magistrate/Trial Court and the trial has begun, re-investigation/further investigation is not permissible. The High Court refused the prayer for further investigation /re-investigation of FIR No. 120 of 2020 on merits as well as mainly on the ground that once the chargesheet is filed after investigation and the charges are framed, the Magistrate has no jurisdiction to order further investigation / re-investigation / de novo investigation.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The original writ petitioner (the victim), feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the High Court's judgment and order, preferred an appeal to the Supreme Court (Criminal Appeal No. 13 of 2023). The Supreme Court was asked to determine whether the High Court was justified in denying the relief of transfer of the investigation to the CBI and refusing to order further investigation / re-investigation / de novo investigation. The Supreme Court confirmed the High Court's refusal to transfer the investigation to the CBI, but partly allowed the appeal regarding further investigation.

directions: The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court refusing to transfer the investigation of the FIR No. 120 of 2020 to CBI is hereby confirmed.
The investigation is hereby quashed and set aside and we direct / permit the State investigating agency to further investigate into the FIR bearing No. 120 of 2020.

Further investigation be carried out and completed as early as possible, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the present order and the further supplementary report be placed before the learned Magistrate in the Trial/before the concerned Trial Court thereafter forthwith, which may be considered by the Trial Court in accordance with law and on its own merits and the accused be tried accordingly and in accordance with law and on merits.

issue.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in denying the relief of transfer of the investigation to the CBI?

facts: The appellant filed a writ petition in the High Court, alleging that the police investigation was biased and conducted in a 'sham and casual manner'.
The appellant requested that the investigation be transferred to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
The High Court denied this request, partly because a chargesheet had already been filed and charges had been framed against the accused.
The appellant appealed the High Court's decision to the Supreme Court.
law: The power to transfer an investigation to the CBI is an extraordinary power that courts should exercise only 'sparingly' and in 'rare and exceptional cases'.
Such exceptional cases may include situations where high officials are involved or where the investigation is found to be prima facie tainted or biased.
application: The Supreme Court reviewed the facts and circumstances of the case in light of the established legal principles.
The Court found that the case did not meet the high threshold of being a 'rare and exceptional case' that would justify a transfer to the CBI.
The Court also noted that the appellant's own lawyer did not 'vehemently press' for the transfer during the Supreme Court hearing.
Based on these considerations, the Court found itself in 'complete agreement' with the High Court's decision on this specific matter.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the High Court had not committed any error and was justified in denying the relief of transferring the investigation to the CBI. It therefore confirmed (upheld) that part of the High Court's judgment.

issue.issue_text: Whether a constitutional court has the power to order further investigation, re-investigation, or de novo investigation after the charge sheet has been filed and the trial has commenced?

facts: The case involved a High Court decision that had dismissed a petition to transfer an investigation, partly on the grounds that a charge sheet had already been filed and charges framed, meaning the trial had begun.
The Supreme Court was asked to decide on the general legal principle of whether a constitutional court's power to order further investigation is barred once a trial commences.
law: A victim has a fundamental right to a fair investigation and a fair trial.
A fair trial is difficult to achieve without a fair investigation.
Constitutional courts are vested with the power to order fresh, de novo, or re-investigation to ensure a fair and just investigation.
Citing the cases of Dharam Pal and Bharati Tamang, the court affirmed that this constitutional power exists to do complete justice.

In rare and exceptional circumstances, such as when high officials are involved or the investigation is tainted, a court can transfer the investigation to an independent agency like the CBI to prevent a miscarriage of justice.
application: The Court reasoned that the commencement of a trial, including the filing of a charge sheet and the framing of charges, cannot be an "absolute impediment" to the exercise of this constitutional power.
The Court argued that if the start of a trial could block further investigation, an accused person might try to have charges framed quickly specifically to prevent a fair and complete investigation.
Allowing the trial's commencement to act as a bar would lead to a "travesty of justice" and undermine the victim's fundamental right to a fair investigation.

Therefore, the court concluded that to ensure a fair trial and complete justice, its power to order further, re-, or de novo investigation must persist even after the trial has started, if the facts of the case warrant it.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that a constitutional court does have the power to order further investigation, re-investigation, or de novo investigation even after the charge sheet has been filed and the trial has commenced. This power is essential to ensure a fair investigation and trial, uphold the victim's rights, and prevent a miscarriage of justice.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in denying the relief of transfer of the investigation to the CBI?
appellant_arguments: The investigation was flawed as relevant evidence, such as the Call Detail Records (CDR) of the appellant's mobile, was not collected.
respondent_arguments: No case is made out for a CBI transfer because the investigation is concluded, chargesheets have been filed, and the Trial Court has already framed the charges.
Since the charges have been framed, the trial has begun, and therefore the case should not be transferred to the CBI.
The appellant's allegation of suffering grievous injuries is not supported by any record or document and was raised for the first time.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a constitutional court has the power to order further investigation, re-investigation, or de novo investigation after the charge sheet has been filed and the trial has commenced?
appellant_arguments: The State itself has admitted in a counter affidavit that further investigation under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C. is necessary and required on certain relevant and material aspects.
The State has specifically admitted lapses in the investigation and that further investigation is needed.
Given the State's admission, the investigating agency should be permitted to conduct a further investigation.
respondent_arguments: The investigation is concluded and the trial has begun as charges have been framed, implying the investigation stage should not be reopened.

cases.case_name: Bharati Tamang Vs. Union of India and Ors.
cases.principle: For the principles culled out from it and other decisions regarding the necessity of a fair, just, and impartial investigation.

cases.case_name: Dharam Pal Vs. State of Haryana and Ors.
cases.principle: For its observation and holding after taking into consideration a catena of decisions on the point of further investigation.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The judicial power to transfer a criminal investigation is an extraordinary power that must be used sparingly and only in exceptional circumstances.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court concluded that while the circumstances of the case did not meet the high threshold of being "exceptional" to warrant a transfer of the investigation to the CBI, its constitutional duty to ensure a fair investigation and trial necessitated ordering a further investigation by the state agency. The Court affirmed its power to issue such a direction even after a trial has commenced, as the stage of the proceedings cannot be an absolute impediment to preventing a miscarriage of justice.
legal_tests_applied: The power to transfer an investigation must be used “sparingly” and only “in exceptional circumstances”.

The constitutional courts can direct for further investigation or investigation by some other investigating agency to ensure a fair investigation and a fair trial, and the commencement of a trial cannot be an absolute impediment for exercising this constitutional power.
why_appellant_lost: The Court was in complete agreement with the High Court's decision to refuse the transfer of the investigation to the CBI, finding that the high threshold for exercising this "extraordinary power" was not met.
The Court noted that the appellant's counsel had not vehemently pressed the prayer for a CBI transfer.
why_respondent_won: The Court affirmed the High Court's decision not to transfer the case to the CBI, reasoning that the power to transfer an investigation is an extraordinary one that must be used sparingly and only in exceptional circumstances.
policy_considerations: The endeavour of the Court should be to have the fair investigation and fair trial only.
The purpose is, there has to be a fair investigation and a fair trial. The fair trial may be quite difficult unless there is a fair investigation.
It is the duty of the Court to ensure that full and material facts are brought on record so that there might not be miscarriage of justice.
The purpose of justice commands that the cause of the victim... deserves to be answered so that miscarriage of justice is avoided.
